lifestyle_note: large genome, versatile environmental and opportunistic pathogen
confusable_with: other Pseudomonas species (P. putida group, P. fluorescens group)
why_it_matters_for_detection: Large genome means more reads per cell than small-genome organisms in a read-share profile. Closely related Pseudomonas absorb its reads when the reference is thin.

lifestyle_note: gut commensal; some lineages are pathogens
confusable_with: Shigella (same species by genome similarity), Escherichia albertii
why_it_matters_for_detection: By k-mers E. coli and Shigella are near-identical, so a species label cannot separate harmless from pathogenic lineages. Needs gene or strain-level follow-up.

confusable_with: Escherichia coli (distant but shares many k-mers), other S. enterica subspecies
why_it_matters_for_detection: A species call says nothing about serovar or virulence. Serovar-level questions need dedicated typing.

lifestyle_note: gut and food lactic acid bacterium, renamed Limosilactobacillus fermentum in 2020
why_it_matters_for_detection: Small genome plus the name change: databases disagree on the label, so strict string matching undercounts it. Aliases are listed in config/aliases.tsv.
Genus-level agreement is easy, species-level less so when relatives are in the database.

lifestyle_note: skin and nose carrier, opportunistic pathogen
confusable_with: other staphylococci (S. argenteus, S. schweitzeri, coagulase-negative species)
why_it_matters_for_detection: Very low-abundance S. aureus in the log mock (0.000089 percent) is below what 2 million reads can show at all; do not read its absence as a method failure.

confusable_with: Listeria innocua, L. ivanovii and other Listeria
why_it_matters_for_detection: Many reads stop at genus level because Listeria species share most of their k-mers (218,000 reads at genus versus 13,000 at species in this repo's even-mock run).

confusable_with: Bacillus spizizenii (former subspecies), Bacillus cereus group (which includes the anthrax agent)
why_it_matters_for_detection: Naming trap: every tool here labels the isolate B. spizizenii. The B. cereus group (cereus, thuringiensis, anthracis) is so close genomically that species labels from short reads are not a reliable way to tell them apart. Spores also resist DNA extraction, so wet-lab recovery can be low.

gram_or_wall: thick glucan and chitin cell wall
why_it_matters_for_detection: Eukaryote: absent from bacteria-only databases such as Kraken2 standard, so its reads are forced onto wrong bacteria or a human call. Tough cell wall lowers extraction yield, so yeast is under-represented in DNA from cells.

confusable_with: Cryptococcus gattii and other basidiomycete yeasts
why_it_matters_for_detection: Largest genome in the mock and not in bacteria-only databases: 74 to 90 percent of its reads were pushed into Pseudomonas in this repo's Kraken2 runs. Capsule and wall make extraction harder.
